note: Track intervals-on-neck (guitar-scales), step 4, on guitar-play-along's interval shape with walk "note": from Do on the D string, a 5th up and a 5th down, then a 4th up and a 4th down, then both intervals in turn from Do on the A string. Every note the text names is in the line and Do is ringed. The why says what the two intervals share, so the learner can try the same with a 3rd and a 6th. It states its moves (any key, tempo 60 to 90) and mentions no selector.

exercise.title: A 5th and a 4th, up and down from one note
exercise.why: A 5th up and a 4th down from one note land on the same note name, an octave apart, so learning both from one place gives you two ways to reach the next note of a tune.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the backing track at {{=bpm}}, and play along from the tab. Every pair starts on {{1}} on the D string: first up a 5th to {{5}} on the G string, then down a 5th to {{4}} on the A string.
Play until your hand goes to both notes without hunting for them.

Press Play below to start the backing track. From the same {{1}}, a 4th up is {{4}} on the G string and a 4th down is {{5}} on the A string.
They are the two notes from before, each an octave away from where you found it.

Press Play below to start the backing track. Now {{1}} is on the A string and both intervals come in turn: the 5th up and down, then from a new bar the 4th up and down.
In another key {{1}} moves to another fret, and the other notes keep their places around it.
